title: Amalgamation of Companies
outcomes: Distinguish amalgamation, absorption and external reconstruction.
Compute purchase consideration and exchange ratios.
Close the books of the transferor company.
Record the amalgamation in the transferee's books, including inter-company adjustments.

meta.exam_tip: Compute purchase consideration first, then prepare realisation, shareholders' and transferee entries in that order.

concepts.title: Amalgamation, absorption and external reconstruction
body: In an amalgamation two or more companies combine: either a new company is formed to take over existing ones, or an existing company absorbs one or more others (absorption).
External reconstruction is when a new company is formed to take over an existing company's business, usually to restructure it.
For accounting, AS 14 classifies amalgamations as being in the nature of merger (pooling of interests method) or purchase (purchase method).
concepts.analogy: Whatever the legal form, the accounting follows merger or purchase.
concepts.work: A newly formed company taking over a struggling company's business is an external reconstruction.

concepts.title: Computing purchase consideration and exchange ratios
body: Purchase consideration is the payment to the transferor's shareholders in shares, securities, cash or other assets.

Methods: lump sum (stated amount); net payment (sum of all payments to shareholders); net assets (agreed value of assets taken over less liabilities taken over); and intrinsic value (number of shares based on each company's value per share).
Intrinsic value per share = net assets available to equity shareholders ÷ number of equity shares. The exchange ratio is the transferor's value per share divided by the transferee's value per share.
Payments to debenture holders and creditors, and liquidation expenses borne by the transferee, are not part of purchase consideration.
concepts.analogy: Value both companies per share; the ratio decides how many new shares are issued.
concepts.work: If a transferor share is worth ₹60 and a transferee share ₹40, each transferor share gets 1.5 new shares.

concepts.title: Closing the books of the transferor company
body: The transferor closes its books through a realisation account: assets (except cash if retained) are transferred at book values to its debit; liabilities taken over to its credit; purchase consideration is credited with a debit to the transferee's account.
Receipt of consideration is debited to shares, securities or bank. Liabilities not taken over are paid; liquidation expenses are debited to realisation (if borne by the transferor).

Share capital and reserves are transferred to equity shareholders' account; profit or loss on realisation also goes there. Preference shareholders are paid as agreed, any difference going to realisation.
Finally, shares and cash received are distributed to shareholders, closing all accounts.
concepts.analogy: Realisation account collects everything; shareholders' account settles the rest.
concepts.work: Fictitious assets like preliminary expenses are transferred to the equity shareholders' account, not realisation.

concepts.title: Entries in the books of the transferee company
body: Purchase method: the transferee debits "Business purchase" and credits the liquidator of the transferor with the consideration; it then records assets and liabilities at agreed values, with goodwill or capital reserve for the difference. Statutory reserves are recorded against an Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve.
Pooling method: assets, liabilities and reserves are recorded at book values; the difference between consideration and transferor's share capital is adjusted in reserves.
Shares issued are recorded at nominal value plus premium; liquidation expenses paid by the transferee are debited to goodwill (or capital reserve) under the purchase method.
The post-amalgamation balance sheet is prepared in Schedule III format with notes.
concepts.analogy: The transferee records what it bought and what it paid.
concepts.work: Shares issued at ₹12 (face ₹10) credit share capital ₹10 and securities premium ₹2 per share.

concepts.title: Inter-company holdings, debts and unrealised profit
body: Inter-company owings (debtors and creditors, bills) are cancelled in the transferee's books after amalgamation.
Unrealised profit on goods sold between the companies still in stock is removed from stock against reserves or the goodwill/capital reserve.
If the transferee holds shares in the transferor, consideration is paid only to outside shareholders; the investment is cancelled, its cost compared with the share of net assets.
If the transferor holds shares in the transferee, those shares are part of assets taken over and may be cancelled or reissued as agreed.
concepts.analogy: Remove everything the two companies owed or earned from each other.
concepts.work: If the transferee already owns 20% of the transferor, only the other 80% receive consideration.

jobs.title: Amalgamation working papers
jobs.situation: Your company is absorbing a sister company; the scheme fixes an exchange ratio and agreed asset values.
steps: Compute purchase consideration and shares to be issued.
Prepare realisation and shareholders' accounts for the transferor.
Record assets, liabilities, goodwill or capital reserve in the transferee.
Eliminate inter-company debts and unrealised profit.
jobs.takeaway: Two sets of books close and open in one transaction.

mcqs.q: In the transferor's books, purchase consideration is credited to:
mcqs.explain: The transferor debits the transferee (purchasing company) and credits realisation account with the purchase consideration, as part of working out profit or loss on realisation. In practice: then receive the shares or cash.
mcqs.topic: Closing the books of the transferor company

mcqs.q: Preliminary expenses of the transferor at amalgamation are transferred to:
mcqs.explain: Fictitious assets such as preliminary expenses are not transferred to the transferee; they reduce what belongs to equity shareholders and are debited to their account. In practice: close them first.
mcqs.topic: Closing the books of the transferor company

mcqs.q: Intrinsic value per share of A ₹50 and of B ₹25. For each share of B, A issues:
mcqs.explain: Exchange ratio = value of B share ÷ value of A share = 25 ÷ 50 = 0.5, so each B share gets half an A share. In practice: fractional entitlements are settled in cash.
mcqs.topic: Computing purchase consideration and exchange ratios

mcqs.q: Under the net assets method, purchase consideration equals:
options: Agreed value of assets taken over less liabilities taken over
mcqs.explain: The net assets method values the business taken over as the agreed values of assets less the liabilities taken over, which equals the consideration. In practice: exclude fictitious assets.
mcqs.topic: Computing purchase consideration and exchange ratios

mcqs.q: Liquidation expenses of the transferor paid by the transferee (purchase method) are debited to:
options: Profit and loss of the transferor
mcqs.explain: Under the purchase method, liquidation expenses borne by the transferee are part of the cost of acquisition and debited to goodwill or set against capital reserve. In practice: the transferor makes no entry if it bears nothing.
mcqs.topic: Entries in the books of the transferee company

mcqs.q: Inter-company debts between the amalgamating companies are:
mcqs.explain: After amalgamation, the debtor and creditor are the same company, so the mutual owings are cancelled by a contra entry in the transferee's books. In practice: reconcile balances first.
mcqs.topic: Inter-company holdings, debts and unrealised profit

mcqs.q: Stock ₹36,000 bought from the transferor at cost plus 20%. Unrealised profit:
mcqs.explain: Profit included = 36,000 × 20/120 = ₹6,000, which is removed from stock against reserves or goodwill/capital reserve. In practice: use margin on selling price.
mcqs.topic: Inter-company holdings, debts and unrealised profit

mcqs.q: If the transferee already holds 30% of the transferor's shares, consideration is paid to:
mcqs.explain: A company does not pay itself; consideration goes only to outside shareholders, and the transferee's existing investment is cancelled against its share of net assets. In practice: adjust goodwill.
mcqs.topic: Inter-company holdings, debts and unrealised profit

mcqs.q: Assets ₹20 lakh (book), liabilities taken over ₹6 lakh, consideration ₹12 lakh, no expenses. Realisation shows:
mcqs.explain: Net assets transferred at book value are ₹14 lakh; consideration ₹12 lakh is ₹2 lakh less, a loss on realisation borne by equity shareholders. In practice: post it to their account.
mcqs.topic: Closing the books of the transferor company

options: A new company formed to take over an existing company's business
mcqs.explain: In external reconstruction a new company is formed to take over the business of an existing company, which is then wound up; internal reconstruction happens without liquidation. In practice: accounting is similar to absorption.

summary: PC methods: lump sum, net payment, net assets, intrinsic value.
Transferor: realisation account, shareholders account, final distribution.
Transferee: business purchase, assets and liabilities, goodwill/capital reserve.
Cancel inter-company owings; remove unrealised profit.
Pay only outside shareholders where shares are cross-held.
remember: Fictitious assets go to shareholders, not realisation.
traps: Debenture holders are not paid out of purchase consideration.

quickref.v: Lump sum · net payment · net assets · intrinsic

viva.q: What are the methods of computing purchase consideration?
viva.model: Lump sum, net payment, net assets and intrinsic value (exchange ratio) methods.

viva.q: How does the transferor close its books?
viva.model: Through a realisation account for assets and liabilities taken over and consideration, and an equity shareholders account that receives capital, reserves, realisation profit and the final distribution.
The number of transferee shares given for one transferor share, equal to the transferor's value per share divided by the transferee's value per share.
They are cancelled against each other in the transferee's books after amalgamation.

viva.q: What happens to unrealised profit on inter-company stock?
viva.model: It is removed from the stock value and debited to reserves or adjusted against goodwill or capital reserve.

cases.title: Asha Ltd. absorbs Bhakti Ltd.
cases.case: Asha Ltd. absorbs Bhakti Ltd. (purchase method). Bhakti has 2,00,000 equity shares; Asha agrees to issue 1 share of ₹10 at ₹15 for every 2 Bhakti shares and pay ₹1 per Bhakti share in cash. Bhakti's net assets at agreed values are ₹16,50,000.

mcqs.explain: Shares: 1,00,000 × ₹15 = ₹15,00,000; cash: 2,00,000 × ₹1 = ₹2,00,000; total ₹17,00,000 under the net payment method. In practice: value shares at the issue price.
mcqs.topic: Computing purchase consideration and exchange ratios

mcqs.explain: Consideration ₹17,00,000 exceeds net assets ₹16,50,000 by ₹50,000, recorded as goodwill under the purchase method. In practice: amortise it.
mcqs.topic: Entries in the books of the transferee company

mcqs.explain: 1,00,000 shares issued at ₹5 premium each give ₹5,00,000 of securities premium; ₹10,00,000 goes to share capital. In practice: record both credits in one entry.
mcqs.topic: Entries in the books of the transferee company
